scenarios.name: heating_air_leaves_warmer_than_it_arrived
scenarios.description: Healthy OS#1 operation: 15 °C mixed air leaves at 25 °C after the fan and an active heating coil. The gap runs negative, which no `>` against a positive threshold can satisfy

scenarios.name: sensor_spread_absorbed_by_threshold
scenarios.description: SAT reads 2 °C below MAT — inside the combined eSAT + eMAT − dTSF band, so a pair of sensors at their rated accuracy plus a fan that adds less rise than assumed cannot fire the rule

scenarios.name: cooling_coil_leaking_through_heating
scenarios.description: SAT 6 °C below MAT while the unit is in heating: a leaking or stuck-open cooling coil valve is stripping more heat than the fan and heating coil put in. Alarms one alarm_delay (1800 s) after the condition appears

scenarios.name: dx_stuck_on_deep_gap
scenarios.description: SAT 10 °C below MAT — DX cooling stuck on against a heating call. Same verdict as a leaking valve; the rule reports the contradiction, not which device caused it

scenarios.name: gap_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge: mat − sat = 3.0 °C exactly. `gapBig` is a strict `>`, so a gap sitting precisely on mat_sat_gap_threshold reads healthy — G36's `<=` would call this a fault

scenarios.name: gap_just_over_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge, other side: mat − sat = 3.1 °C clears the strict comparison and alarms after alarm_delay

scenarios.name: no_temperature_rise_is_not_this_fault
scenarios.description: SAT equals MAT — the heating coil is contributing nothing, which is a real problem and not this one. The gap is zero, so this rule stays silent and the finding belongs to the inactive-coil rules

scenarios.name: transient_gap_clears_before_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: a 6 °C gap opens at load and closes at t = 1200 s as the hot-water loop comes up to temperature. Twenty minutes is short of alarm_delay, so nothing alarms

scenarios.name: oscillating_gap_never_persists
scenarios.description: Honesty case for the instantaneous-sampling deviation: SAT alternates every 600 s between 6 °C below MAT and 2 °C above it. The mean sits outside the band, so G36's 5-minute rolling average would fault; persistence resets on every compliant tick and this rule never does

scenarios.name: fault_clears_on_recovery
scenarios.description: A sustained 6 °C gap alarms at 1800 s; the leaking cooling valve is isolated at t = 3000 s and SAT climbs above MAT, dropping the alarm on that tick — TrueDelay has no off-delay
